sections.label: Aims of amendment Bill
sections.summary: The amendments seek to help MUIS administer its functions, let ROMM and SYC digitalise, and improve SYC divorce administration.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Broadly, the amendments seek to: first, enable MUIS to better administer its functions and duties to support the Muslim community; second, enable the ROMM and SYC to adopt new digitalisation processes; and third, enhance the administrative provisions relating to SYC for more effective outcomes for families who go through a divorce.

sections.label: MUIS creating wakaf
sections.summary: The Bill lets MUIS create a wakaf itself, unlike traditional wakaf, and makes the WMS a community endowment fund.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Unlike traditional wakaf which must be created by Muslim individuals and scoped for specific religious charitable purposes by the bequeathed upon their death, this amendment Bill will enable MUIS, as an Islamic body, to create a wakaf on its own; and for the WMS to serve as a community endowment fund for social and religious development.

sections.label: Fatwa Committee membership expanded
sections.summary: The Bill expands the Fatwa Committee's membership from four to eight full members to support its work.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: To support the work of the Fatwa Committee, this amendment Bill will expand the Committee's membership from four to eight full members.

sections.label: Defining Muslim religious schools
sections.summary: The Bill defines Muslim religious schools, gives MUIS inspection powers, and sets a 14-day appeal period to the Minister.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: While the AMLA states that it is the function and duty of MUIS to administer all Muslim religious schools in Singapore, the definition of such institutions has never been prescribed in law.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Hence, this amendment Bill will introduce a definition of Muslim religious schools, provide for inspection powers for MUIS officers, as well as specify a fixed period of 14 days for an appeal to be made to the Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs.

sections.label: Digital Certificates of Marriage
sections.summary: The Bill allows ROMM to introduce digital Certificates of Marriage for Muslim marriages to facilitate e-services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: To facilitate the implementation of e-services for marriage solemnisation, this amendment Bill will allow ROMM to introduce digital Certificates of Marriage for Muslim marriages.

sections.label: MUIS wakaf creation powers
sections.summary: The Bill gives MUIS powers to create a wakaf, the legal foundation for the Wakaf Masyarakat Singapura.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: First, to provide MUIS with the powers to create a wakaf.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: This will form the overarching legal foundation for the creation of the Wakaf Masyarakat Singapura (WMS) to serve the long-term religious and social needs of our Muslim community.

sections.label: Wakaf, halal assurance, religious schools
sections.summary: WMS will be created by MUIS as a community wakaf, imported halal products get greater assurance, and a definition for Muslim religious schools is established.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: In the same spirit and principle, WMS will be created by MUIS as a community wakaf to serve our socio-religious needs in the long-term.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Second, to provide Muslim consumers and businesses with greater assurance when purchasing imported halal products.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Third, to improve the quality of Islamic religious education in Singapore by establishing a definition for Muslim religious schools that MUIS is to regulate.

sections.label: AMLA amendments for Muslim institutions
sections.summary: The Bill seeks to ensure AMLA reflects contemporary needs and includes amendments on wakafs, foreign halal certification bodies, Fatwa Committee, Muslim religious school definition and unattributable contributions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Fifth, amendments will be introduced to support ROMM’s and SYC's efforts to strengthen the services they provide to Muslim families. : Mr Speaker, in conclusion, this Bill seeks to ensure that the AMLA continues to reflect the contemporary needs of our Muslim community and will enable our Muslim institutions to better administer their functions to support these needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It includes amendments that enable the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (MUIS) to carry out its role to support the Muslim community more effectively, such as empowering MUIS to create wakafs, recognition of Foreign Halal Certification Bodies, expanding the membership of the Fatwa Committee, introducing a definition of Muslim religious school, and a clarification on unattributable contributions to the Mosque Building and MENDAKI Fund.

sections.label: Equipping future religious leaders
sections.summary: Future religious leaders must be equipped to guide the community on complex issues, so the speaker supports amendments enabling MUIS to create wakafs for future funding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Our future religious leaders must be adequately equipped to guide the community in navigating complex issues such as meat created in a lab that was recently given a fatwa, stem cells and ongoing social debates on current issues, just to name a few.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, I support the amendments to AMLA which will enable MUIS to create wakafs to provide additional sources of funding to meet future needs of the Muslim community in Singapore.

sections.label: Recognition of foreign halal bodies
sections.summary: The passage states that the second point concerns the recognition of Foreign Halal Certification Bodies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Second, on the recognition of Foreign Halal Certification Bodies (FCHBs).

sections.label: AMLA amendment Bill objectives
sections.summary: The amendment Bill aims to enable MUIS to improve administration, improve ROMM and SYC digital processes, and enhance Syariah Court administration provisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I welcome the diligence and hard work that was done to continue improving Singapore's Administration of Muslim Law Act (AMLA) for the benefit and progress of the Muslim community in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This amendment Bill has several objectives, firstly, to enable the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (MUIS) to improve its administrative work and the management of its functions and responsibilities to support the Muslim community; second, to further improve the quality of the digital processes of the Registry of Muslim Marriages (ROMM) and Syariah Court (SYC); and third, to further enhance the provisions to administer the Syariah Court in order to achieve a more effective outcome.

sections.label: Muslim religious school framework
sections.summary: The Minister is asked about the framework to reinforce the existing one, with Muslim religious school covering those habitually providing Islamic instruction to 10 or more individuals in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Looking ahead, can the Minister share, in general, the framework that will be created to further reinforce the existing framework?

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Those that are referred to as "Muslim religious school" includes individuals or organisations that habitually provides Islamic instruction to 10 or more individuals physically present in Singapore and secondly, a place where 10 or more individuals are physically present in Singapore are habitually provided with Islamic instruction.

sections.label: Reason for number 10
sections.summary: The passage asks why the number 10 was chosen and whether there is a specific reason.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My question on this is, why is the number 10 is chosen, and is there any specific reason?

sections.label: Wakaf accounts for specific causes
sections.summary: The passage suggests developing wakaf accounts dedicated to specific causes or social service sectors so donors can choose where donations go.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To address this situation, may I suggest we develop wakaf accounts dedicated to specific causes, such as education or healthcare or targeted at specific social service sectors, such as those working with children or women, thereby allowing individuals and families to donate to a cause of their choice, and to know that their donation will be distributed in accordance with their wishes.

sections.label: MUIS wakaf investment and governance strategies
sections.summary: The passage seeks clarification on MUIS strategies to navigate market fluctuations, safeguard investment returns, sustain wakaf long-term, and ensure accountable and transparent governance.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As wakaf funds held by MUIS are managed like other investments, thereby exposing them to market risks, I seek clarification about the strategies MUIS has in place to navigate market fluctuations, safeguard returns on investments and secure the long-term sustainability of wakaf.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I also seek clarification about the strategies MUIS has in place to ensure the effective, accountable and transparent governance and administration of the wakaf system.

sections.label: Islamic instruction scheme scope and purpose
sections.summary: The scheme applies to anyone providing Islamic instruction to non-family members and was established in 2017 to enhance religious teachers' standing and serve as a reference.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The scheme applies to anyone providing Islamic instruction to one or more persons who are not members of his or her family, and was established in 2017 to enhance the standing of religious teachers and to serve as a credible source of reference for the Singapore Muslim community.

sections.label: Judge-led approach to divorce support
sections.summary: The proposed judge-led approach accelerates commitment, empowers judges to initiate support for individuals experiencing trauma due to divorce, and facilitates swift marriage dissolution.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The proposed judge-led approach accelerates this commitment and empowers judges to proactively initiate support for individuals experiencing trauma due to divorce and facilitate a swift and smooth dissolution of marriage.

sections.label: Judge-led approach and divorce clarification
sections.summary: The judge-led approach aims to strengthen emotional and psychological well-being during divorce, and the passage seeks clarification on expediting dissolution while ensuring a fair legal process.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The judge-led approach aims to further strengthen the emotional and psychological well-being of individuals undergoing trauma during divorce.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Related, I seek clarification about whether these provisions within the judge-led model to expedite the dissolution of marriage to minimise the prolonged emotional distress for individuals involved, while still ensuring a fair and just legal process?

sections.label: Amendments to Muslim legal framework
sections.summary: The amendments on wakaf, foreign halal certification bodies, Muslim religious schools and the Legal Committee reinforce a dynamic legal framework respecting religious teachings.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The amendments, particularly those related to wakaf, recognition of Foreign Halal Certification Bodies, definition of Muslim religious schools and expansion of the Legal Committee collectively reinforce the idea of a dynamic legal framework.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This framework not only respects religious teachings but also encourages independence of thought, decision-making and contributions to the greater good of both the Muslim community and Singapore as a whole.

sections.label: Legal Committee opinion waiting time
sections.summary: The resident was told the Legal Committee may take one or two years to give an opinion due to its volume of requests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The resident was informed that the Legal Committee may take one or two years to provide an opinion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The resident was informed that this is because of the volume of requests that the Legal Committee has to handle.

sections.label: Recognising foreign halal certification bodies
sections.summary: The question asks what considerations decide whether recognition is granted to a foreign halal certification body.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To ensure that equally stringent standards continue to apply to halal food sold in Singapore, can Minister share what are the considerations for deciding whether to grant recognition to a foreign halal certification body?

sections.label: Wakaf created by Majlis
sections.summary: The member has two clarifications on proposed section 58(3A) about wakaf to be created by the Majlis.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, on wakaf, I have two clarifications in relation to the proposed section 58(3A), on the proposed wakaf to be created by the Majlis.

sections.label: Oversight of recognised foreign halal bodies
sections.summary: The member asks whether section 88AA(6) covers all foreign halal certification bodies and what safeguards MUIS has over recognised ones.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In total, as of 15 January 2024, I note, on the MUIS website, that there are 99 entities registered on the list of FHCBs recognised by MUIS, including state halal authorities and private entities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, may I clarify if the proposed amendments of section 88AA (6) are limited to the misuse of halal certificates and marks relevant to FHCBs only registered and recognised by MUIS, or would these cover all FHCBs, even those that are not currently recognised in MUIS' list?

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, may I ask what are the safeguards and extent of oversight that MUIS has over recognised FHCBs to the extent that one can ensure that these FHCBs, especially private FHCBs, upkeep their standards of halal certification overseas and are not compromised as a result of cost and profit pressures?

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These safeguards would be an important assurance for members of the public to ensure that sources of food certified halal, locally or overseas, remain trusted for consumption.

sections.label: Digital marriage certificate and community wakaf
sections.summary: The amendments digitalise the marriage certificate in ROMM and provide legislative infrastructure for the Singapore Community Wakaf.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The amendments also bring greater ease of use through the digitalisation of the marriage certificate in the ROMM and the legislative infrastructure to support the enactment of the Singapore Community Wakaf, or the Wakaf Masyarakat Singapura (WMS).

sections.label: Syariah Court children maintenance jurisdiction
sections.summary: Section 35(ca) extends Syariah Court jurisdiction to maintenance of minor children, but the Syariah Appeal Board referred such proceedings to the Family Justice Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The expansion of jurisdiction of the Syariah Court in section 35(ca) now includes custody, care and control, access or maintenance of minor children on divorce or nullification of marriage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In a recent decision, the Syariah Appeal Board held that proceedings in the Syariah Court do not and will not deal with children’s maintenance, and whoever wishes to commence such proceedings shall be referred to the Family Justice Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hence, if the Syariah Court jurisdiction now covers “maintenance of minor children”, what will be the process for applying for such maintenance?

sections.label: Syariah Court matrimonial asset jurisdiction
sections.summary: In TMO v TMP the Syariah Court refused division of matrimonial assets, and the Court of Appeal held it retained residual jurisdiction to avoid a legal vacuum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For instance, in the case of TMO v TMP, the Syariah Court refused to grant an order for division of matrimonial assets because it did not have jurisdiction under AMLA since the Syariah Court did not decree the divorce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Court of Appeal held that it retained residual jurisdiction over matters not falling within the jurisdiction of the Syariah Court, in order to avoid a legal vacuum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: An amendment to AMLA to empower the Syariah Court to make decisions on such issues like these will help Muslims from having to go to two different, separate Courts, which will be both time-consuming and costly.

sections.label: First multi-asset wakaf by MUIS
sections.summary: The WMS is unique as the first multi-asset wakaf created by MUIS receiving voluntary contributions from all Singapore Muslim community members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The WMS is unique as it will be the first multi-asset wakaf created by MUIS where voluntary contributions from all members of the Singapore Muslim community can be received.

sections.label: WMS supports mosques and community
sections.summary: The WMS augments the MBMF for capital expenditure on land lease renewals, redevelopment, upgrading and new mosques, and serves as a reserve fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The WMS will therefore augment the existing Mosque Building and MENDAKI Fund, or MBMF, to support the large capital expenditure needed to fund the various land lease renewals, redevelopment and upgrading, as well as to develop new mosques.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: WMS will serve as a reserve fund to support the community in moments of need, such as during severe national crises like the COVID-19 pandemic.

sections.label: Registration for habitual religious instruction
sections.summary: Individuals or organisations offering religious instruction habitually to at least 10 individuals physically present in Singapore must register as a Muslim religious school with MUIS under the IECP scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Second, any individual or organisation seeking to offer religious instruction habitually to at least 10 other individuals physically present in Singapore – that means, together, not one at a time, 10 together, up to 10, would have to register as a Muslim religious school with MUIS, under its current Islamic Education Centres and Providers, or IECP, scheme.

sections.label: IECP curriculum verification requirements
sections.summary: IECPs must submit their school curriculum, syllabus and learning materials for verification and quality assessments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: IECPs, therefore, must submit their school curriculum, syllabus and learning materials for verification and quality assessments.

sections.label: Fatwa Committee decision power
sections.summary: The amendment empowers the Fatwa Committee to decide whether a fatwa is needed based on the request received.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: With the amendment, the Fatwa Committee will be empowered to decide whether there is a need to issue a fatwa based on the request received.

sections.label: FHCB halal recognition assessment
sections.summary: FHCBs will undergo rigorous assessment to ensure their halal standards are comparable with MUIS' standards for MUIS recognition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: FHCBs will then be subjected to a rigorous assessment to ensure that their halal standards are comparable with MUIS' standards, in order to be granted recognition by MUIS.

sections.label: FHCB audit and delisting
sections.summary: During the three-year recognition period, FHCBs face MUIS audit; non-compliant FHCBs may be suspended or delisted and their products barred.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: During the three-year recognition period, these FHCBs will be placed under MUIS' audit and surveillance regime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: FHCBs that fail to comply with MUIS' requirements could be suspended or delisted from MUIS' recognition list and their certified products cannot be used by MUIS' halal-certified companies.

sections.label: Syariah Court child maintenance jurisdiction
sections.summary: Amendments to AMLA section 35 clarify the Syariah Court's jurisdiction includes child maintenance on divorce or nullification of marriage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: First, on the amendments to clarify the Syariah Court’s jurisdiction in clauses 8 and 12 of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We are amending section 35 of the AMLA to clarify that the Syariah Court’s jurisdiction includes maintenance of children on divorce or nullification of marriage, which has always been part of section 52(3) of AMLA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The Family Justice Courts, or FJC, will continue to hear child maintenance matters.

sections.label: Strengthening legal foundation for Muslim institutions
sections.summary: Passing this amendment Bill further strengthens the legal foundation for statutory Muslim institutions to build the Muslim Community of Success.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: With the passing of this amendment Bill, we will further strengthen the robust and contemporary legal foundation for our statutory Muslim institutions to build our Muslim Community of Success.
